exampleAnswers.title: Negating a Predicate Expressed in Plain English

question.text:
$\qquad$ $5$ divides $x.$

The predicate $P(x)$ is given above. Which of following represents $\neg P(x)?$
question.explanation:
The symbol "$\neg$" represents negation. So, our task is to negate the given sentence.

To negate our plain English sentence, we place the words "It is not true that" in front of it. This gives the following:

$\qquad$ It is not true that $5$ divides $x.$

In other words, $5$ does not divide $x.$ Therefore, $\neg P(x)$ means the following:

$\qquad$ $5$ does not divide $x.$

example.title: Finding the Truth Set of Predicate's Negation

question.text:
Find the truth set of $\neg P(x)$ given the following predicate defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

$\qquad$ $P(x):$ $x - 7 \lt -9$
question.explanation:
The truth set of $\neg P(x)$ is the complement of the truth set of $P(x){:}$ \[ T_{\neg P} = \overline{T}_P \]

To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} x- 7 & \lt -9\\[5pt] x & \lt -2 \end{align*}

So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P = (-\infty,-2). $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_{\neg P} &= \overline{T}_P \\[5pt] &= \overline{(-\infty,-2)} \\[5pt] &= [-2,\infty). \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Truth Set of Predicate's Negation

question.text:
Find the truth set of $\neg P(x)$ given the following predicate defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

$\qquad$ $P(x):$ $3x + 2 \gt 8$
question.explanation:
The truth set of $\neg P(x)$ is the complement of the truth set of $P(x){:}$ \[ T_{\neg P} = \overline{T}_P \]

To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} 3x + 2 & \gt 8\\[5pt] 3x & \gt 6 \\[5pt] x & \gt 2 \end{align*}

So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P = (2,\infty). $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_{\neg P} &= \overline{T}_P \\[5pt] &= \overline{(2,\infty)} \\[5pt] &= (-\infty,2]. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Truth Set of Predicate's Negation

question.text:
Find the truth set of $\neg P(x)$ given the following predicate defined over the universal set of positive integers between $1$ and $10,$ inclusive:

$\qquad$ $P(x):$ $x$ is prime
question.explanation:
The truth set of $\neg P(x)$ is the complement of the truth set of $P(x){:}$

\[ T_{\neg P} = \overline{T}_P, \]

The truth set of $P(x)$ is the set of primes between $1$ and $10,$ inclusive, i.e., \[ T_P = \big\{ 2,3,5,7 \big\}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_{\neg P} &= \overline{T}_P \\[3pt] &= \overline{\big\{ 2,3,5,7 \big\}} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 1,4,6,8,9,10 \big\}. \end{align*}
